subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Hydrogen Combustion Engine
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Hydrogen Combustion Engine usable.

hook.text: Hydrogen burns cleanly and powerfully, producing nothing but water vapor from the exhaust.

buildup.text: BMW, Toyota, and others have tried burning hydrogen in modified gasoline engines.

discovery.text: Hydrogen combustion still uses pistons and crankshafts—it just swaps the fuel for a cleaner one.

twist.text: Hydrogen is extremely hard to store, needing either high-pressure tanks or cryogenic cooling.

climax.text: Toyota's hydrogen Corolla raced at Le Mans to prove the concept could handle extreme demands.

punchline.text: Burning hydrogen is easy—storing it is the hard part.

quiz.question: What comes out of a hydrogen combustion engine's exhaust?
